gaps.sentence: The wedding guests ___ when the string quartet began to play.
gaps.hint: in progress when the music began
gaps.explanation: An action in progress when a past event occurred takes the past continuous: were still arriving.

gaps.sentence: What ___ in the garage? I can hear drilling.
gaps.hint: can hear shows evidence happening now
gaps.explanation: The present evidence of noise shows something in progress now, so the present continuous fits: is going on.

gaps.sentence: This is the best pizza I ___ in years.
gaps.hint: superlative experience counted up to now
gaps.explanation: Superlative statements about experience up to now take the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: By the time you read this letter, I ___ the country.
gaps.explanation: An action completed before a future point takes the future perfect: will have left.

gaps.sentence: The play ___ when we reached the theatre, so we missed the first scene.
gaps.hint: it started before we reached it
gaps.explanation: The starting happened before the past moment of arriving, so the past perfect fits: had already started.

gaps.sentence: When you ___ John tomorrow, please give him my regards.
gaps.hint: no will after when for the future
gaps.explanation: In time clauses referring to the future, English uses the present simple, not 'will': see.

gaps.sentence: They ___ so much since they started the new school.
gaps.hint: since they started with present result
gaps.explanation: Change measured from a past starting point to now takes the present perfect: have grown.

gaps.sentence: He ___ the same bus to work every morning, even in winter.
gaps.hint: every morning signals a fixed routine
gaps.explanation: 'Every morning' describes a fixed routine, which takes the present simple: catches.
